blocks.summary: Enables EIGRP on interfaces matching a network statement.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS IP Routing: EIGRP Command Reference

parameters.name: wildcard-mask
parameters.description: Optional inverted mask for more precise matching

content.fieldNotes: Without a wildcard mask, this matches the entire classful network — usually worth specifying one for anything but the simplest lab setup.

blocks.title: traceroute
blocks.summary: Shows the hop-by-hop path packets take to a destination.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS IP Routing Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
1  192.168.1.1  4 msec  4 msec  4 msec
2  10.0.0.2     8 msec  8 msec  8 msec
content.fieldNotes: Use once ping fails or succeeds unexpectedly and you need to know which specific hop the path breaks at.

blocks.title: ping
blocks.summary: Tests basic reachability to a destination using ICMP echo.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS IP Addressing Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
Sending 5, 100-byte ICMP Echos to 10.10.10.5, timeout is 2 seconds:
!!!!!
Success rate is 100 percent (5/5)
content.fieldNotes: Usually the very first command run in any connectivity troubleshooting — establishes whether the problem is reachability at all before looking anywhere more specific.

blocks.title: telnet
blocks.summary: Opens a Telnet session to a remote device, or tests a specific TCP port.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS Fundamentals Command Reference

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Optional TCP port — a common trick for testing whether a specific port is open/listening

content.fieldNotes: Telnet itself is insecure and shouldn't be used for actual remote management (use SSH) — but as a quick 'is this port open' test it's still genuinely useful.

blocks.title: show spanning-tree
blocks.summary: Shows spanning-tree state, root bridge, and port roles.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS LAN Switching Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
VLAN0010
  Root ID    Priority 4096
             Address   0011.2233.4455
Gi0/1  Root FWD 19  128.1  P2p
content.fieldNotes: Check port roles/states here whenever a switched network is doing something unexpected after a topology change — a port stuck in blocking is a common surprise.

blocks.title: show ip dhcp conflict
blocks.summary: Lists IP addresses the DHCP server detected as already in use when it tried to assign them.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS IP Addressing: DHCP Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
IP address      Detection method  Detection time
10.10.10.50     Ping              Jul 26 2026 09:00 AM
content.fieldNotes: A nonempty list here is a strong signal of a static IP colliding with the DHCP pool, not a DHCP server malfunction.

blocks.title: show ip nat statistics
blocks.summary: Shows NAT configuration summary and translation activity counters.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS IP Addressing: NAT Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
Total active translations: 12
Outside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/0
Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/1
content.fieldNotes: Confirms inside/outside interfaces are actually assigned as expected — a common NAT misconfiguration is simply having them backwards.

blocks.title: show ip interface
blocks.summary: Shows detailed per-interface IP configuration, including which ACLs are applied.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS IP Addressing Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up
  Outgoing access list is 101
  Inbound  access list is not set
content.fieldNotes: Not the same as show ip interface brief — this is the detailed version, and it's the fastest way to confirm which ACL is actually applied to an interface and in which direction.

blocks.title: terminal monitor
blocks.summary: Sends console log/debug output to the current terminal (SSH/Telnet) session.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS Network Management Command Reference

content.fieldNotes: Without this, debug output only appears on the physical console — a very common 'why isn't debug showing anything' question over SSH.

blocks.title: debug ip packet
blocks.summary: Traces IP packets processed by the router in real time.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS Network Management Command Reference

parameters.name: access-list
parameters.description: Optional ACL number to limit output to matching traffic only

content.fieldNotes: Genuinely dangerous on a busy production router without an access-list filter — unfiltered, it can generate enough output to spike CPU and make the device unresponsive.

blocks.title: undebug all
blocks.summary: Turns off all active debug output.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS Network Management Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
Router# undebug all
All possible debugging has been turned off
content.fieldNotes: Run this immediately after any debug session — forgetting to turn off debug on a production device is a well-known way to cause a self-inflicted outage.

blocks.title: show version
blocks.summary: Shows IOS version, uptime, hardware, and the last reload reason.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS Fundamentals Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
Cisco IOS Software, Version 15.2
Router uptime is 4 weeks, 2 days
Last reload reason: power-on
content.fieldNotes: After any unplanned outage, the 'last reload reason' line is often the fastest way to tell whether a device crashed, lost power, or was reloaded intentionally.

blocks.title: show logging
blocks.summary: Displays the contents of the logging buffer and current logging configuration.

sourceOfTruth.title: Cisco IOS Network Management Command Reference

content.sampleOutput:
Syslog logging: enabled
*Jul 26 14:02:11: %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet0/2, changed state to down
content.fieldNotes: This is usually the first command to run when something changed and nobody knows why — the timestamped events often show the root cause directly.
